notes.markdown:
A redesigned MonoPhone app and web console, SIP that works on restricted networks, more control over the call
assistant, new automation steps for CRM, WhatsApp and calendars, and safer editing in the API.

## New

- **A redesigned MonoPhone app.** The app now has four tabs: **Calls**, **Messages**, **People** and **Keypad**. Calls
  and voicemail share one list (All, Missed, Voicemail), People holds your team, the company phonebook and your own
  contacts with favourites and a VIP switch, and your photo at the top opens **Me**, where every personal setting is
  grouped by what you want to do. Phone numbers are written the way people in your country write them.
- **A new call screen.** A waiting or held call stays visible at the top, the controls sit in a tidy grid, a small
  icon shows the connection quality, and tablets show the caller's card beside the call.
- **Call assistant roll-out.** Turn the assistant on for a department or the whole company (Admin, Call assistant),
  optionally so people cannot switch it off. Each person gets a notification when their assistant is turned on. The
  console also has a shared assistants page, editable rules under My assistant and a "Screen with AI first" option on
  ring groups.
- **Call assistant on your phone.** A call assistant widget shows whether the assistant is on, paused or out of budget
  (iPhone Home Screen and Lock Screen, Android home screen). On iPhone the live screening banner is driven by the
  server, and a Focus filter can switch the assistant mode while a Focus is on.
- **AI budgets page.** Set spending limits for AI use in one place (Admin, AI, AI budgets).
- **More automation steps.** WhatsApp messages can be free text inside the 24-hour window, with a template as
  fallback. Kommo, Bitrix24 and Odoo can create contacts, leads and tasks and update deals. Automations can use the AI
  assistants' Google and Microsoft 365 calendars. Click-to-call can ring a group or queue first.
- **More caller languages.** The assistant follows callers in 28 more common languages.
- **Instagram and Apple Messages for Business.** Both are now described in the guides, and Apple Messages connects
  through your messaging provider.
- **A new web console.** One sidebar replaces the top bar, the long More menu and the separate admin menu. **Home**,
  **Calls**, **Messages** and **People** are the same four places as in the app, and **Me** (your name at the bottom of
  the sidebar) holds your personal settings. Press **Ctrl K** (Cmd K on a Mac) to find any page, person, queue or ring
  group and jump to it. On phones the sidebar becomes a tab bar with a Keypad tab.
- **Home shows what needs you.** Missed calls grouped by caller with Call back, new voicemail with a transcript line,
  unread team chats and customer conversations, plus today's numbers, favourites and your queues.
- **Calls, Messages and People are one list each.** Call history, voicemail and recordings share one Calls list with a
  detail panel; team chat, customer conversations, SMS and fax share Messages; the directory, your team, contacts and
  customers share People. Old addresses open the new pages.
- **A redesigned web phone.** The phone is docked at the right edge of the page (it collapses to a thin strip, and
  becomes a sheet or full screen on small windows). One search finds colleagues, contacts, the company phonebook, queues
  and groups. An incoming call shows a card on any page, and the call screen has a waiting-call card, a held-call row,
  a call-quality icon and a tidy control grid, like the app.
- **The admin console in eight sections.** Overview, People and devices, Numbers and trunks, Call handling, Contact
  centre, Messaging, AI, Monitoring and reports, and Settings, with at most seven entries each. Related pages are tabs of
  one page. Every old address still works. Call flows (menus, call flows, automations and personal flows) are one list
  with a Type filter.
- **An admin status board.** The Overview shows live tiles (calls now, agents, queue waits, phones online, trunks,
  licence seats), **Needs attention** with a Fix button that opens the exact page, **Live now**, calls per hour against
  the same weekday last week, and recent changes with who made them.
- **Standard lists and a Save bar.** Lists across the admin console share one look: live search, filter chips kept in
  the address, sortable columns, a "..." menu on each row, bulk actions, Show more, and cards on phones. Settings pages
  share a sticky **Save bar** that shows unsaved changes.
- **Restricted networks.** Desk phones on networks that block or break SIP can register with **SIP over TLS on port
  443**, shared with the web console, or through the **built-in VPN** with a certificate per phone. Switch either on or
  off in the console (Admin, Restricted networks), run the built-in checks, and choose the network path per device;
  provisioning profiles are included for all supported desk phone brands.
- **Widgets and Live Activities.** MonoPhone has widgets for favourites, missed calls, voicemail, your status (one tap
  for Do not disturb), the call assistant and, for supervisors, the live queue, on iPhone and Android. iPhone adds Lock
  Screen versions, an administrator widget and Live Activities for a call in progress and for call screening. Widget
  names and labels follow the language of the phone.
- **eSIM in MonoPhone.** My eSIMs (Settings) shows when each eSIM was last seen, lets you switch mobile data on or off
  for sponsored eSIMs, and a notification opens My eSIMs straight away when an administrator makes an eSIM ready to
  install.
- **MonoPhone extras.** Connect your Google account from the app (Me, Account), import and export the company phonebook
  as CSV with a preview, and on Android show messages in your language and summarise a recorded call, both on the phone itself.
- **Video and screen-share links for customers.** From the phone panel (More, Video link) or a conversation, send a
  customer a link by SMS, in the conversation or by e-mail. The customer opens it in a browser with no app and no
  account, agrees to the notice, and talks face to face or shares their screen. The agent can record the session only
  with the customer's consent. Links expire after 30 minutes by default and a session lasts at most four hours.
- **Website widget with an AI button.** On a live chat channel routed to an AI agent, visitors get an AI button, and the
  host page is told when it opens, a message is sent and a reply arrives (never the text). New per-channel protection:
  hCaptcha or Turnstile, a visitor address read through your trusted proxies, and a chat transcript mailed only when the
  visitor asks.
- **Extension sign-in for every user.** The click-to-call browser extension now signs in with single sign-on for any
  user, not only roles that control other people's calls; it can only place calls from your own extension.
- **Pictures in text messages.** MMS pictures show in the console and in MonoPhone, and are kept with the conversation.
- **Apple Watch transfers and call waiting.** The watch app can transfer a call (blind or attended), handle a second
  call (answer and hold the first, swap, end), and reports call quality.
- **More integrations.** Zendesk and ServiceNow connect with sign-in instead of pasted tokens. Calendly and a second booking tool,
  ServiceTitan, Jobber, Zendesk, Freshdesk and ServiceNow events reach automations, the call assistant's own bookings
  raise appointment events, and a field-service job can give the number to call. Kommo and Bitrix24 log calls (with the
  recording link) and show e-mail, phone and company in the pop-up.
- **Company SIEM export and lead list.** A company can send its audit events to its own SIEM, with a health check and a
  dropped-events alert. Real-estate and clinic leads have their own list under Admin, Integrations.
- **More telephony.** A silenced number routed to a ring group goes to the group's no-answer destination without
  ringing. Queues skip agents in Do not disturb unless the caller is a VIP, and callback numbers are checked against the
  do-not-call lists before every attempt. Callers refused for the simultaneous-call limit hear a spoken message. A
  media session that loses its port is moved to a new one in a live call. Hot-desk and conference prompts have audio in
  all nine languages, and IVR input hand-offs can send headers and map the answer.
- **More messaging.** Meta channel tokens are watched and an alert appears seven days before they expire. Template
  messages can be sent again after the 24-hour window. Chinese, Japanese and Thai conversation search finds whole words.
  A reached SMS cap also notifies administrators on their phones. Call keypad shortcuts (send a digit while on a call)
  can be chosen in the web console and in MonoPhone.
- **Platform.** Terraform can read a device's SIP credentials without keeping them in state, the PBX answers the relay's
  proof-of-work request on enrolment, and a Helm chart and cloud image sources are included.
- **More for administrators.** Trunk forms control how inbound calls are identified (number, caller and host); queue
  pause, wrap-up and available times are kept for reports; an assistant's desk phone gets a key for each executive;
  Cisco phones follow the company language; exported recordings say whether the caller heard the recording notice;
  storage compliance holds now work on Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob; and a language chosen in a call flow menu
  reaches live translation.
- **The console finished everywhere.** The **Calls** hub has more filters (direction, dates, number or extension, tag),
  one Export menu and a row menu (add contact, block, create a Jira issue, save or delete a recording). Call history,
  voicemail and recordings are standard lists with a player in the row. Chat has one search box and a "+" for a new
  chat, and the inbox shows one icon and one badge per conversation and opens the first conversation on wide screens.
  Contacts have an empty state with **Add contact** and **Import CSV**.
- **Supervisor control.** Listen, Whisper and Barge are one segmented control, and each agent's state is a pill with a
  Status menu.
- **Reports with tabs, tiles and a chart.** Extensions, Queues, Quality and Scheduled are tabs, with tiles for the
  period, a ranking chart, a totals row and a column picker.
- **Settings home with search.** Search finds pages, settings and their usual names, and each category lists its
  sections with **Open here** (the real form) or **Open full page**.
- **Numbers and trunks.** Numbers show **Where it rings**, with an empty state that offers **Add your first number**,
  and each trunk has a status card (state, latency and channel limit).
- **Agent login and logout codes moved to Dial codes** (Settings, Telephony). Queues links to the new place.
- **Toasts with Undo, a globe language menu and your photo on Me.** Short confirmations offer **Undo**, the sign-in page
  has a globe menu to choose the language, and the Me button shows your photo.
- **Upgrades help without a shell.** The Upgrades page explains how to update from the server's command line with a
  copy button and a link to the guide.
- **MonoPhone sign-in and forms.** First sign-in leads with **Scan QR code**. Forms have labels above fields and are
  grouped into sections, the Me page is reorganised by what you want to do, pages show skeleton placeholders while
  loading, there are new dialogs, the supervisor pages follow the redesign, and one icon set is used everywhere.
  Call assistant counters show on the assistant pages.
- **Redesigned Apple Watch and Wear OS apps.** Both have Calls (recent calls and voicemail, with All, Missed and
  Voicemail on Apple Watch), People, Keypad and Me. Numbers are formatted like on the phone, Me offers Available, Busy
  and Do not disturb, and "Ready" shows only when something needs fixing. Apple Watch shows a compact call-waiting
  card and a slim held-call row, and both watches follow larger text sizes.

## Improved

- **Licence sign-up in the setup wizard is checked end to end.** Signing up, confirming your e-mail, signing in and
  receiving the trial licence with its end date are now tested automatically on every build, against a real licence
  service.
- **Console lists and forms everywhere.** Settings pages (Security, Recording, Logging, Transcription limits, Storage,
  Backups, Companies, AI settings, Integrations) share the sticky **Save bar**, and many more pages (Calling profiles,
  Door phones, Hotel, Hot desking, Park slots, Shared voicemail, Phonebook, Executives, Backups, Legal holds, Languages,
  Support, Export jobs, Partners, Companies, Device extras and others) use the shared list with search, filters, a "..."
  row menu, empty and error states, and cards on phones. Forms that sat beside a list now open in a dialog.
- **One page header and calmer status colours.** Every page uses the same heading, with its actions beside it. Status
  chips no longer use call-green or hang-up-red: enabled and failed states use the accent and warning colours.
- **Dark mode, phone width and readability.** Colours that stayed light in dark mode now follow the theme, dimmed hint
  text is easier to read, and filters, toolbars and forms no longer run off a phone screen in German or Russian.
- **Setup bar.** The set-up box on Overview is one line: steps done, progress, the next step and Continue setup.
- **Calmer colours and keypad in MonoPhone.** Green always means call, red means end or decline, and every switch uses
  the same accent colour. Lists show placeholders while loading and say clearly which list failed.
- **Readiness and forwarding.** Call readiness shows only what needs fixing. Forwarding has a quick set-up (ring my
  mobile too, voicemail after 20 seconds, forward everything).
- **Paging a group no longer rings members twice.** Members that answer join the page once.
- **Failed secure SIP connections** are now listed with the reason next to other unattributed failures, and incoming
  caller-certificate revocation lists are checked.
- **Safer concurrent editing in the API.** More settings now require the current version when you change them and
  refuse an out-of-date edit, and long lists are paged (see the API guide).
- **Media sessions survive a restart** of the media service, including call recordings.
- **Keyboard shortcuts.** `l`, `m` and `c` now open Calls, Messages and People. Custom bindings of shortcuts that no
  longer exist are reset to the defaults. Old console addresses (history, voicemail, recordings, chat, inbox, SMS) redirect to
  the new pages and keep their filters.
- **Clearer colours, names and numbers in the console.** Green is only for call and answer, red only for hang up,
  decline and missed. Phone numbers are written the way people in your country write them, names come before numbers,
  times are relative, and empty values show a dash instead of a raw placeholder. Loading lists show placeholders.
- **API conventions (for API users).** Changing a stored setting requires the current version in `If-Match` (the server
  answers 428 when it is missing and 412 when it is out of date) and returns a new `ETag`. More lists use cursor paging
  (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`), including music-on-hold playlists, Jira call-log entries and the new call groups
  list. If your integration edits settings or reads long lists, check the API guide. A new status board endpoint backs
  the Overview.
- **Notifications** show phone numbers grouped for every country, and a paged group keeps members that were woken by a
  push as listeners.
- **Assistant translation.** Each assistant can turn live translation of its phrases on or off, and translated phrases
  are cached per company. The call page can summarise a call on the phone from its transcript.
- **AI.** The WhatsApp confirmation template is checked when you save, and conversation search finds old segments
  without a database extension.
- **Standard lists and Save bars on every remaining page.** The last raw tables use the shared list, and the remaining
  settings forms use the sticky **Save bar**.
- **A distinct success colour.** Successful and enabled states use their own colour, separate from call-green.
- **A stricter, more accurate API description.** The API document now states the length, range and pattern limits the
  server enforces, and documents more responses (for example a 201 on first save and 429 on chat routes). For API
  users: optional query parameters are no longer nullable (a null used to be sent as the text "null"), and a storage
  destination requires a name.

## Fixed

- **Disk filling up over time.** The analytics database kept its own internal diagnostic logs forever, which could
  fill a small server's disk and block upgrades. It now keeps them for 7 days, and an upgrade clears old ones before
  it checks for free space.
- **File dialogs closing.** Choosing a file again, or cancelling the file chooser, no longer closes the whole dialog (a
  second contacts import lost its dialog).
- **Saving the Company step of setup** was refused when the country also changed the time zone; it now saves.
- **Menus in lists** closed on their own right after being opened by an automated click or a small scroll; they stay open.
- **Waiting calls on the call screen** were drawn under the buttons on small phones; they are now always visible.
- **Installing a personal call-assistant template** for someone without an assistant no longer shows a misleading
  message.
- **Several setting pages** showed raw `undefined` or untranslated placeholders; they now show a dash or a clear message.
- **Failed secure SIP connections** are now kept for 30 days per company, so the list survives a restart.
- **Group paging** no longer drops a member that registers late after a push wake.
- **Call flow designer behind the docked phone.** At narrower window widths the canvas, palette and properties panel
  ran under the phone panel; the designer now adapts to its own width.
- **Setup wizard** no longer refuses the Company step on a fresh install, and the Extension step is covered by tests.
- **Searches containing a null character** returned a server error; they now answer with a clear validation error.
- **Partner routes** now answer errors in the same format as every other route.
- **Fax received label** showed a raw key instead of its name; it is translated in all nine languages.

## Security

- Security fixes (low): the certificate of an incoming secure trunk call is now also checked for revocation (OCSP).
- Security fixes (low): the browser extension's sign-in no longer asks for control over other people's calls.
- Security fixes (low): video-link tokens are stored only as a hash, expire quickly and are rate limited, and a web
  chat widget can require a captcha.
- Security fixes (low): the e-mail library is updated to fix several published advisories (STARTTLS handling,
  message formatting and panics), and other dependencies are updated, including a web networking library.

**API conventions (for API users).** Changing a stored setting requires the current version in `If-Match` (the server answers 428 when it is missing and 412 when it is out of date) and returns a new `ETag`. More lists use cursor paging (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`), including music-on-hold playlists, Jira call-log entries and the new call groups list. If your integration edits settings or reads long lists, check the API guide. A new status board endpoint backs the Overview.
**Notifications** show phone numbers grouped for every country, and a paged group keeps members that were woken by a push as listeners.

**Assistant translation.** Each assistant can turn live translation of its phrases on or off, and translated phrases are cached per company. The call page can summarise a call on the phone from its transcript.
**AI.** The WhatsApp confirmation template is checked when you save, and conversation search finds old segments without a database extension.
**Standard lists and Save bars on every remaining page.** The last raw tables use the shared list, and the remaining settings forms use the sticky **Save bar**.
**A distinct success colour.** Successful and enabled states use their own colour, separate from call-green.

**A stricter, more accurate API description.** The API document now states the length, range and pattern limits the server enforces, and documents more responses (for example a 201 on first save and 429 on chat routes). For API users: optional query parameters are no longer nullable (a null used to be sent as the text "null"), and a storage destination requires a name.

**Disk filling up over time.** The analytics database kept its own internal diagnostic logs forever, which could fill a small server's disk and block upgrades. It now keeps them for 7 days, and an upgrade clears old ones before it checks for free space.
**File dialogs closing.** Choosing a file again, or cancelling the file chooser, no longer closes the whole dialog (a second contacts import lost its dialog).
**Saving the Company step of setup** was refused when the country also changed the time zone; it now saves.
**Menus in lists** closed on their own right after being opened by an automated click or a small scroll; they stay open.
**Waiting calls on the call screen** were drawn under the buttons on small phones; they are now always visible.
**Installing a personal call-assistant template** for someone without an assistant no longer shows a misleading message.
**Several setting pages** showed raw `undefined` or untranslated placeholders; they now show a dash or a clear message.
**Failed secure SIP connections** are now kept for 30 days per company, so the list survives a restart.
**Group paging** no longer drops a member that registers late after a push wake.
**Call flow designer behind the docked phone.** At narrower window widths the canvas, palette and properties panel ran under the phone panel; the designer now adapts to its own width.
**Setup wizard** no longer refuses the Company step on a fresh install, and the Extension step is covered by tests.
**Searches containing a null character** returned a server error; they now answer with a clear validation error.
**Partner routes** now answer errors in the same format as every other route.
**Fax received label** showed a raw key instead of its name; it is translated in all nine languages.
Security fixes (low): the certificate of an incoming secure trunk call is now also checked for revocation (OCSP).
Security fixes (low): the browser extension's sign-in no longer asks for control over other people's calls.
Security fixes (low): video-link tokens are stored only as a hash, expire quickly and are rate limited, and a web chat widget can require a captcha.

Security fixes (low): the e-mail library is updated to fix several published advisories (STARTTLS handling, message formatting and panics), and other dependencies are updated, including a web networking library.

notes.summary: A redesigned MonoPhone app and web console, SIP that works on restricted networks, more control over the call assistant, new automation steps for CRM, WhatsApp and calendars, and safer editing in the API.
